candidates.explanation: Best guess. The seeded admin is inserted directly with role id RoleEnum.admin. Later admins are created through this method. Its role validation and assignment is where a later admin could end up with the wrong role or no role. The stored role would then not match what the Roles guard expects, and the guard returns 403. I could not see the rest of the method, the guard or the JWT strategy, so this is not confirmed.

This maps the domain role to the persistence entity when a user is created. If the role is built or dropped incorrectly here, an admin created after the seed gets a different role than the seeded one. Their JWT would then carry a role the Roles guard rejects.
This builds the role claim in the JWT payload. If the claim is derived wrongly, tokens for later admins would fail the RolesGuard check. I could not see the method body, so this is unconfirmed.

fix.description: In UsersService.create, validate createUserDto.role.id against the numeric RoleEnum values and assign the role as { id: Number(createUserDto.role.id) }. Make sure the persisted role id is the same numeric value the Roles guard compares against (RoleEnum.admin = 1). Also check that the guard and JWT payload do not depend on the user's id or on any other property that only the seeded account has.

candidates.explanation: Best guess. The seeded admin is inserted directly with role id RoleEnum.admin. Later admins are created through this method. Its role validation and assignment is where a later admin could end up with the wrong role or no role. The stored role would then not match what the Roles guard expects, and the guard returns 403. I could not see the rest of the method, the guard or the JWT strategy, so this is not confirmed.

This maps the domain role to the persistence entity when a user is created. If the role is built or dropped incorrectly here, an admin created after the seed gets a different role than the seeded one. Their JWT would then carry a role the Roles guard rejects.
This builds the role claim in the JWT payload. If the claim is derived wrongly, tokens for later admins would fail the RolesGuard check. I could not see the method body, so this is unconfirmed.

fix.description: In UsersService.create, validate createUserDto.role.id against the numeric RoleEnum values and assign the role as { id: Number(createUserDto.role.id) }. Make sure the persisted role id is the same numeric value the Roles guard compares against (RoleEnum.admin = 1). Also check that the guard and JWT payload do not depend on the user's id or on any other property that only the seeded account has.
